'''MEI''' ('''Mathematics in Education and Industry''') is an independent educational charity and [[curriculum development]] body for [[mathematics education]] in the United Kingdom. Income generated through its work is used to support the teaching and learning of mathematics.

==History==
MEI was founded in 1963 with a grant from the Schools & Industry Committee of the [[Mathematical Association]]. In 1965 it produced its first exam, [[Additional Mathematics]], then produced an A level course two years later. MEI's A-level exams were the first to include [[Probability theory|probability]].

It was incorporated as a company on 18 October 1996.

==Structure==
Although independent, MEI works in partnership with many organisations, including the [[Her Majesty's Government|UK Government]]. MEI is a [[registered charity]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://beta.charitycommission.gov.uk/charity-details/?regid=1058911&subid=0|title=Registered Charity no. 1058911|website=Charity Commission|language=en|access-date=3 July 2017}}</ref> with a [[board of directors]] and a small professional staff.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://mei.org.uk/|title=MEI|website=mei.org.uk}}</ref>

==Qualifications==
* [[GCE Advanced Level|GCE AS/A level]] Mathematics, Further Mathematics and Further Mathematics (Additional) (Published by [[Oxford, Cambridge and RSA Examinations|OCR]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://mei.org.uk/syllabus|title=MEI > Teachers > AS/A level Mathematics/Further Mathematics Curriculum 2005 (legacy)|website=mei.org.uk}}</ref>)
* AS Level Statistics
* [[GCSE]] Mathematics
* Foundations of Advanced Mathematics (FAM) – a freestanding course
* Introduction to Quantitative Methods (in association with OCR<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://mei.org.uk/quantitative_methods|title=MEI > Teachers > Quantitative Methods|website=mei.org.uk}}</ref>)
* OCR MEI Level 3 Core Maths Qualifications (Level 3 Certificate in Quantitative Reasoning and Level 3 Certificate in Quantitative Problem Solving)<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://mei.org.uk/core-maths-qualifications|title=MEI > Teachers > Core Maths Qualifications|website=mei.org.uk}}</ref>

==Competitions==
MEI organises an annual online competition called Ritangle<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://integralmaths.org/ritangle/|title=Ritangle - an Integral maths competition|website=integralmaths.org}}</ref> for teams of students of [[A level]] Mathematics, the [[International Baccalaureate]] and [[Scottish Highers]]. Questions are posted on the Integral website, with correct answers releasing a clue for the final question.
